Write in full sentences where explanations are required.

context.title: Case study: Kagiso's party
context.text: Kagiso (16) is popular and wants to keep his place in his group of friends. At a weekend party, older boys bring alcohol and dagga. Kagiso's girlfriend, Naledi, says she wants to go home, but Kagiso's friends mock him: 'A real man doesn't let his girlfriend tell him what to do.' Kagiso drinks heavily and later pressures Naledi to stay. A friend offers to drive them home, although he has also been drinking.

questions.prompt: Identify THREE risky behaviours in the case study.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): underage drinking; drug use; pressuring a partner; ignoring consent/boundaries; getting into a car with a drunk driver

questions.prompt: Explain how the friends' comment reflects a harmful gender stereotype, and its possible effect on Naledi.
questions.memo:
✓ It suggests men should control women / make decisions (1)
✓ It pressures Kagiso to dominate rather than respect Naledi (1)
✓ Naledi's choices and safety are disregarded; risk of abuse (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how alcohol increased the danger in this situation.
questions.memo:
✓ It impaired Kagiso's judgement and lowered inhibitions (1)
✓ making pressure or coercion more likely (1)
✓ and the drunk driver puts lives at risk (1)

questions.prompt: What should Naledi and Kagiso have done to stay safe? Give FOUR suggestions.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): leave when uncomfortable; respect each other's decisions; refuse alcohol/drugs; arrange a safe lift with a parent; never ride with a drunk driver; stay with trusted friends; call for help

questions.prompt: Name TWO places where Naledi could get help if Kagiso becomes controlling or abusive.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428; Childline 116; police; school counsellor; trusted adult

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Rights, careers and the environment

questions.prompt: Name TWO Chapter 9 institutions and describe the role of each.
Explain why freedom of expression does not allow hate speech.
questions.memo:
✓ Rights can be limited if reasonable and justifiable (section 36) (1)
✓ Hate speech violates others' dignity and equality (1)
✓ and can incite violence (1)

questions.prompt: Describe FOUR study habits that will help a learner succeed in Grade 10.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): timetable; active study methods; spaced revision; past papers; enough sleep; ask for help; limit distractions

questions.prompt: Discuss TWO environmental problems in your community and suggest one solution for each.
Explain THREE ways in which healthy self-esteem helps a young person resist negative peer pressure.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): confident to say no; does not need approval; values own goals; makes independent decisions; chooses supportive friends

questions.prompt: Explain how a learner could use the Holland personality types to explore careers.
questions.memo:
✓ Complete an interest questionnaire to find their strongest types (1)
✓ Look at careers linked to those types (1)
✓ Research the requirements of those careers (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE ways young people can participate actively in democracy.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): RCL; register to vote at 16; petitions; peaceful protest; volunteering; youth organisations; contacting councillors
